notes:
NOTES FOR THE ORCHESTRATOR (none is a failed requirement).

(1) Cold-load cause not proven. The e2e log shows warm-up ready with cold start chat 4294 ms and embed 825 ms and a pass. The earlier abstained run without warm-up is consistent with a cold load eating the 8 s deadline (a 4.3 s chat load plus a press that needs about 6 s of work would exceed 8 s), but nothing in the log is an A/B on the same state, and the abstained run's missing notes were not captured here. Plausible, not confirmed. A cheap confirmation would be to run the old code against an already loaded model and see whether it abstains.

(2) Deadline margin is thin. Stage times from the passing run: memory 5266 ms, consistency 3581 ms, assistance 910 ms. Memory and consistency run in parallel, so the critical path is about 5.27 + 0.91 = 6.2 s plus the freeze, leaving roughly 1.8 s before the 8 s deadline (plus MARGIN_S). The log gives no measured press-to-card time, so this is my arithmetic from stage times. If Ollama serialises the two parallel chat requests on the single shared GPU (OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL), the sum is 5.27 + 3.58 + 0.91 = 9.76 s, which exceeds 8 s and would produce a partial card or an abstention at the deadline. One run on a quiet GPU is not a latency claim; a slower GPU turn, a longer conversation or the follow-up call could tip a press into partial. The e2e test only requires answered or partial. This belongs in later latency work, not a T8.7 failure, but it should not be read as comfortable headroom. The token counts (437, 489, 228) suggest memory at about 83 tokens/s.

(3) keep_alive and the shared-GPU rule. CLAUDE.md says to unload any Ollama models you loaded (keep_alive 0) before releasing the GPU. The backend sends keep_alive 30m on every chat and embed request and has NO unload on shutdown: lifespan shutdown stops warm-up, stops background work and flushes telemetry, but never sends keep_alive 0. So when the app (or the e2e test, which builds the production app) exits, both models stay in VRAM for up to 30 minutes unless the person or orchestrator unloads them. The rule is on the one holding the GPU turn, so nothing in the code breaks it, but the 30-minute value is not self-compatible with it: whoever runs the all-real test under ctl gpu-acquire must unload afterwards (ollama stop <model>, or a keep_alive 0 request) before gpu-release. I saw ollama ps empty and 1561 MiB GPU memory in use at the start of my check, so the earlier run was unloaded. A 30-minute keep_alive is reasonable for a person using the app interactively on their own GPU, and it is what keeps presses fast, but it is not honest for a shared GPU unless an unload step is added (for example, an on_shutdown unload, or a documented step in docs/run-everything.md). docs/run-everything.md does not mention this. Recommended follow-up: add the unload to shutdown or the docs.

(4) run_everything.py run from a worktree without a .venv exits with a clear message; it works in the main folder (the .venv is there). The prior failure was the system Python lacking langgraph; the fix selects the .venv Python explicitly.

(5) My pytest runs of files located outside the worktree picked up the main folder's src unless I passed -c pyproject.toml --rootdir=.; I used that for my own tests, so they ran against this commit's code. In-repo runs use the worktree's src via the pyproject pythonpath.

(6) Carried over from the earlier verdict (not re-fixed, not requirements): ContextLensClient.cs Handle() in Unity has no deleted guard for transcript, turn_update or card; the backend cannot send after deleted, so this is defense in depth only, for H3. A press mid-compute when delete runs can still queue its telemetry job after forget(). The telemetry executor thread is non-daemon, so a hung exporter could still delay interpreter exit beyond the bounded flush.

UNCHECKED, belongs to H3 or the person: a real human voice through a physical microphone in a room; browsers other than headless Edge with a fake audio file; Unity at runtime (Editor, XR, WebCamTexture); the pyannote real run with accepted terms and HF_TOKEN on the live path beyond the CPU test of the earlier verdict; the GPU speech service profile; the all-real test was not rerun by me (GPU/Ollama forbidden), I relied on t87_e2e.log and my reading of the test code; the Prometheus path was checked with one gauge, not with the real press metrics under load; the Ollama /api/tags probe in run_everything.py was patched out in my runs, and the production backend was never started by me, so the real backend plus Ollama startup under run_everything.py was not exercised by me.
